newsitem.title: USA: Loctite opens bidding for co, deadline Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: Loctite opens bidding for co, deadline Dec 4.

text.p: Loctite Corp formally set up an auction process to sell itself to the highest bidder, with bids due Wednesday, December 4, a company spokesman said.
"They have created formalized guidelines to make for a fair and uniform bidding process to protect the interests of shareholders," the spokesman said.
To date, the only public bid for Loctite has been a $57.75 per share hostile tender offer from Germany-based Henkel KGaA
Henkel has been a long-time owner of 35 percent of Loctite, and its offer for the balance of the Hartford-based adhesives company is worth about $1.2 billion.
Sources have said Loctite has been approaching potential "white knight" bidders, including DuPont, Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co and Ashland Inc.
The companies have declined to comment.
The Loctite spokesman declined to say what companies will enter bids for Loctite, or the number expected.

But arbitrageurs, the Wall Street traders who specialize in takeover situations, said it was highly unlikey Loctite would open the bidding and set a specific deadline just one week away without beleiving at least one bid would appear to rival that of Henkel.
In ant event, they said, the expectation of of a higher bid -- particularly from Henkel -- has already been discounted by the market as reflected the Loctite's share price.
Meanwhile, a document obtained by Reuters that was prepared for Henkel by their Rothchild Inc investment bankers listed ten potential rival bidders for Loctite.
An "A" group of buyers -- "those most likely to bid" for Loctite -- was composed of Ashland, Elf Aquitaine, 3M, Morton International Inc and Total SA, also of France.
On the "B" list -- those considered less likely to bid for Loctite -- were Akzo Nobel of the Netherlands, Germany's BASF AG, Dow Chemical Co, DuPont and the Anglo-Dutch Unilever.
